flusurvey 1.0
  • Reference

Extract flusurvey data

Source: R/extract_data.r
extract_data.Rd

This extracts flusurvey data for a given number of surveys and years (all by default).

Usage

extract_data(data, surveys = "all", years = "all", join = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

data

either a (named) list of (annual, named) lists of surveys, or (much easier) a filename that contains said list.

surveys

the surveys to extract (e.g., "background", "symptom", "contact" or a combination thereof), "all" for all of surveys that can be found and joinable by merge_data (others are dropped with a warning); surveys that don't exist in all years are dropped too. The order given does not matter. The surveys are always joined in the order background, contact, symptom (see merge_data), with one row per report of the last survey in that order.

years

the years to extract, "all" for all years

join

whether to join the data into one big data.table in the end

...

parameters to be passed to merge_data, especially 'clean' (see documentation of merge_data, by default all cleaning will be performed, set 'clean' to NULL to get the raw data).

Value

a data.table (if join is TRUE) or a list of data.tables (if join is FALSE) with the data

Author

seb

Examples

dt <- extract_data(simulated_data, years = 2013:2014)
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use flag_ill_contacts().
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use flag_ill_contacts().
table(dt$season)
#> 
#> 2012/13 2013/14 
#>    2898    2836 

## without the contact questionnaire
extract_data(simulated_data, years = 2013:2014,
             surveys = c("background", "symptom"))
